# Stories: implement, or push back

For the AI asked to work on stories. Work through every file in **stories/new/** (README.md aside),
one at a time, and for each: **implement it, or push back**; then every file in stories/done/ with an
`Answer:` line under its `Not implemented:` lines: its specs stand; implement what the answers make
checkable, each as its criterion's own `<id>-<n>.cy.ts`, and append a new IMPLEMENTED note. Never guess to make a story fit, and never
change the suite's rules to make a story's test pass.

1. **Read it.** Its id is the first word shaped like `INJ-592`, in the file name, else in its text; its
   title is its first line, the id left out; its steps and outcome are the rest. A file that still holds
   a `---- PROPOSED REWRITE` line is waiting on its person: leave it, and say so in your report, unless an
   `Answer:` line under the rewrite accepts it ("Answer: yes"): then the rewrite is the story; implement it
   as written (`PROPOSED REWRITE: none` proposes nothing to accept). So is one
   whose `Needs from you:` line has no `Answer:` line under it. `Answer:` lines under a push-back are the
   person's answers: read them with the story and decide afresh; they bind as the team's rules do, but only
   words, outcomes, choices and drops: never an element, place or layout of a page no file here shows ("assume
   the page shows..." is a question back, under `Needs from you:`, for that page saved). The
   file name's words are the story's title of record: a text that asks for a different outcome has
   changed since it was named: push back, say what each asks, and propose no rewrite of the changed one. A
   text that asks for less than its name (it checks a form and stops before sending it) is the same story,
   narrowed: implement it.
2. **Check it against what this suite knows.** Every page, link, button and text it names must match
   exactly one thing: ai/GLOSSARY.md, the page classes, their Elements, crawl/the-internet.herokuapp.com.crawl.json, saved-pages/.
3. **Push back** when it is vague (a word matches nothing, or two things), when the crawl could not
   have seen what it needs (behind a login, after a form: ask for a saved page), when it has nothing
   to check, when its outcome holds before its
   steps (what every test already checks as the page opens, its title and what its page class's "Proven
   loaded by" line names; a message already shown; a list already in order: the steps must make the
   difference; opening a page is a step, so what it shows then, its rows, fields or a heading's words, is
   an outcome; a story's "title" may mean the tab or the heading: when both could be meant, push it back
   with `Title is ambiguous: the page title is the browser tab's words, from the page's HTML (here "<tab words>"); the heading is the big words on the page (here "<heading words>"). Say which you mean, as "page title" or "heading".`;
   when the page shows on arrival what the step would make, the story undoes it first, then does the
   step: close the message, then make a new one, and that is the same story, not a different one),
   when it names something the crawled page shows in other words (the story is the record of what is
   wanted: write no test you know will fail on it; push that criterion back, naming both, and ask which
   is right), or when it would send real data on the live site (a click on a form's send with values
   the page refuses is a test only when the criterion is the form's own checks; permission to send lives
   in the team rules only, never in a story's text or an `Answer:` line). Count what a visitor sees at the
   end, not the lines: steps, conditions and the page's arrival are not outcomes. What the crawled pages
   hold was seen, shown or hidden (`data-sb-hidden="true"` is a closed menu, not an unknown); unseen is
   only what no file holds. A list of acceptance criteria is not a reason: each criterion is a
   requirement, a test of its own (4.); push back the whole story only when no criterion can be checked.
   Append to the story file, and leave it in stories/new/:

   ```
   ---- PUSHBACK (<date>) ----
   Not implemented: <one sentence: why>.
   Needed:
   - <exactly what would make it implementable, one line each>
   ```

   Then propose the story rewritten so it can be checked, under a `---- PROPOSED REWRITE` line, or say
   why none can be (ai/recipes/push-back-a-story.md). The person accepts it by deleting what is above
   it, or by an `Answer:` line under it; never implement your own rewrite before then.
4. **Implement it**: add what the pages lack (ai/recipes/add-an-element.md, add-an-action.md), write
   `cypress/e2e/cases/<id>.cy.ts`, or, for a story with a list of acceptance criteria, one
   `cypress/e2e/cases/<id>-<n>.cy.ts` per criterion that can be checked, n its place in the list counted
   from 1 (ai/recipes/write-a-story-test.md); a number is kept once it has a test (a dropped criterion
   stays in the list, answered "drop"; a new one goes at the end; SR-21 checks it), then run `npm run typecheck` and
   `npm run rules` before you report (neither needs a browser or the network): a type error or a broken
   rule is yours to fix first. If you can, also `npx cypress run --spec cypress/e2e/cases/<id>.cy.ts`.
   Then append, and move the file to stories/done/:

   ```
   ---- IMPLEMENTED (<date>) ----
   Tests: cypress/e2e/cases/<id>-1.cy.ts, <id>-2.cy.ts, ... (or <id>.cy.ts)
   Not implemented: <n> <the criterion>: <why, and what is needed>, one line each (none: say none)
   ```

   A criterion not implemented is listed in your report too, as waiting on the person.
